transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-05
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Orchardly CTO), Aisha (Platform), Omar (Security), Sophie (PM)

Summary:
Quick alignment on Orchardly's marketplace listing + on-prem connector pilot: focus areas KMS/HSM integration, VPC connectivity and egress, packaging (helm/airgap), quantization tradeoffs for onprem inference, and acceptance criteria for pilot lab.

Topics covered: KMS integration approaches, networking patterns for marketplace listing (tunnel vs VPC peering), on-prem packaging/helm, model quantization effects on latency, benchmarking plan, SSO/SAML and audit logging requirements, canary/fallback routing for failed nodes.

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Jordan: alright hi everyone thanks for joining um we got about 50 minutes, appreciate you carving time — i'm jordan meyers from redwood, with priya our se — quick roll call?
[00:00:15] Liam: yeah hi liam chen here, cto at orchardly, thanks for setting up.
[00:00:18] Aisha: aisha gomez, platform eng lead.
[00:00:20] Omar: omar rahman, security architect.
[00:00:22] Sophie: sophie le, product.
[00:00:24] Priya: great, i'll jump into architecture, we put a short agenda in the invite, start with KMS and key flow, then networking, packaging, then quantization notes and lab plan. Sound good?
[00:00:33] Liam: sounds good.

[00:01:05] Priya: ok KMS first — two main patterns we've seen: 1) Redwood-managed KMS proxy where customer keys unwrap in their KMS (you retain CMKs) and we get short lived creds, or 2) customer-run KMS in their VPC with an agent that fetches and injects keys into the runtime via a sealed volume. The former is faster to onboard but requires trust overlay and maybe has compliance gaps for some orgs. The latter is preferred for strict onprem/airgapped customers.
[00:01:42] Omar: um our control plane has to not hold unwrapped keys, so pattern two sounds better. we can't have cloud keys leaving the airgapped cluster. what's the agent — is it a sidecar?
[00:01:55] Priya: typically sidecar or init container that does unwrap via the KMS HSM endpoint and writes to a tmpfs mount with proper perms. we have an example helm chart that shows KMS integration, we can share. note — some transcriptions earlier — our docs call it K-M-S but sometimes written as K M S or KMS H S M — the callout is it must support key rotation and envelope encryption.
[00:02:20] Omar: ok rotation and audit logs are must. we need proof for SOC2 type II.
[00:02:25] Jordan: totally — we have an audit log export format and can feed events to your SIEM. we'll share the audit schema.

[00:03:10] Priya: next networking: we discussed options in the doc: 1) VPC peering / private link from your VPC to the Redwood runtime in the marketplace connector; 2) reverse tunnel over TLS where nodes dial out to a known egress; 3) VPN site-to-site. each has tradeoffs — peering lowest latency, but needs cross-account networking and routing. tunnel is easiest for airgapped but adds NAT/egress considerations.
[00:03:40] Aisha: we probably want the tunnel option for initial pilot because our infra team doesn't want cross-account peering until we've validated throughput and cost. what about egress and firewall rules?
[00:03:50] Priya: you'll need outbound to redwood runner endpoints on 443, plus the KMS endpoint. we'll provide a small CIDR list for egress, and a healthcheck port. Also kube-proxy and some helm values to control probes.
[00:04:05] Liam: is there any persistent state flowing to redwood? we want assurance that inference logs or payloads aren't retained beyond the SLA.
[00:04:12] Jordan: by default for private onprem listing, we operate in a split-control mode — control plane metadata only, and telemetry is optional. we can set retention to zero and send audit logs to your syslog collector. We'll add explicit data flow diagram in follow-up.

[00:05:25] Sophie: quick question on marketplace listing process — to be in the marketplace we have to supply a helm chart, a packaging descriptor, and pass a security checklist, correct?
[00:05:34] Jordan: correct — we'll share the packaging checklist. it includes SSO/SAML config, KMS integration notes, billing meter hooks, and the expected volume expectations for the dedicated connector.

[00:06:10] Priya: on packaging — we recommend a helm chart with two flavors: "managed" where redwood operator is allowed to run and a "private" flavor where install is fully customer-controlled with an operator-less helm values set (airgap friendly). The private flavor will include extra flags for disabling telemetry and enabling local KMS sidecar.
[00:06:38] Aisha: will you support images from our internal registry? we need to use our hardened base images.
[00:06:43] Priya: yes images can be pulled from your registry; we provide manifest template and can accept imagePullSecrets as values.

[00:07:20] Priya: moving to quantization — for onprem workloads many customers choose int8 or int4 quant to reduce GPU memory and cost. tradeoff is sometimes a small drop in quality — we have quant profiles and a quality monitor that runs evals against your prompt set.
[00:07:38] Liam: we run an LLM assistant internally that expects high accuracy on domain terms, so quality delta needs to be within our tolerance. can we run A/B with redwood variants?
[00:07:47] Jordan: yes, canary and A/B routing is supported in the runtime. we can route a percent to quantized model and compare outputs on your test prompts. quality monitor will trigger regression alerts.

[00:08:30] Omar: security question — SSO and SAML: we need SAML 2.0 for console access and RBAC integration with our IdP, plus MFA enforcement. is that in the marketplace offering?
[00:08:40] Jordan: yes the console integrates with SAML/SSO; for private connectors we support SAML assertions via your IdP and can map groups to RBAC roles. we'll share our SAML metadata XML and mapping guide.

[00:09:05] Sophie: also want to confirm licensing/usage billing — how does marketplace billing show up? do you support metering connectors?
[00:09:15] Jordan: marketplace listing supports metering hooks. the connector emits token counts and model identifiers to a local usage agent which can be polled by your billing system or we can collect it to marketplace meter if you opt in. For onprem, many customers prefer a pull-based metering file that you upload monthly.

[00:10:20] Priya: ok shifting to lab and benchmarks — proposal: 2-hour lab where we deploy the private helm chart into your dev VPC, run a set of synthetic workloads and your 10 canonical prompts to measure tail latency, p50/p95, token cost, and CPU/GPU utilization. We'll test three model variants: full fp16, int8 quant, and a smaller distilled model.
[00:10:48] Liam: fine — how much infra do we need? single 16GB GPU node or more?
[00:10:55] Priya: depends on sequence length; for short responses a single a100/80gb or two 40gb nodes will give decent throughput. we can also run on gpus you provide. We have continuous batching in the runtime, so we recommend testing at realistic concurrency.

[00:11:35] Aisha: what about KV cache and session affinity — we need per-user session state to avoid re-priming costs.
[00:11:42] Priya: we support local KV cache with optional external redis for cross-node cache. for the marketplace private flavor, we include a postgres-backed cache in the helm values as an option, though redis is recommended for performance. Note — sometimes our transcriber writes K V cache as "K V cash" — sorry just a transcript quirk.

[00:12:20] Jordan: small demo note — priya will walk through the helm values and show the KMS sidecar snippet, but we won't run a live demo now to keep to time.

[00:12:35] Priya: (screen share described) so here's values.yaml excerpt — you can set keyProvider: "external-kms" and provide kms.endpoint, kms.credentialsSecretName, kms.keyId and tls options. There's an enableAudit: true flag. For airgap we have a sealed secret flow using sops.
[00:13:05] Omar: sops is fine, but we use an HSM — do you have an HSM connector?
[00:13:11] Priya: yes we integrate with generic PKCS#11 endpoints and some vendors like Thales/Entrust. we'll list compatibility matrix in the follow-up.

[00:13:45] Liam: can we see the benchmark spreadsheet you use? i want to add our prompts and acceptance criteria columns.
[00:13:51] Jordan: sure — we'll share a google sheet (or a private link) with the columns: prompt, expected tokens, p50, p95, quality threshold, cost per 1k tokens. we'll add a sample of your prompts if you send them.

[00:14:30] Sophie: timeline and success criteria — we're targeting a pilot in Q3 that demonstrates parity on latency and <5% quality regression with quantized variant while keeping unit cost reductions of 30%.
[00:14:40] Jordan: that seems doable; the lab will give us concrete numbers.

[00:15:10] Priya: a few gotchas from other listings: 1) image signing and SBOM for marketplace review, 2) support window for the private connector (we recommend a 12-month minor update cadence), 3) fallback routing — if local nodes fail, we can route to a hosted fallback model (requires data policy acceptance).
[00:15:35] Omar: fallback routing to hosted is a non-starter for our regulated use-case unless we have encryption-at-rest with keys you don't possess.
[00:15:42] Jordan: understood — in that situation we disable fallback and enable canary within your infra only.

[00:16:20] Priya: quick note on billing hook technicals: the connector writes metering lines to /var/log/redwood-meter and we provide a helper to produce a signed usage blob you upload. Alternatively we can run a local metering agent that pushes to your billing collector.
[00:16:45] Aisha: upload model sounds fine, less network chatter.

[00:17:30] Liam: are there any known performance regressions when running quantized models on our target hardware (we're using NVIDIA A10s)?
[00:17:38] Priya: A10s are fine for int8 in most cases; int4 may need specialized kernels and can be slower for certain attention patterns. we'll include kernel/arch recommendations in the runbook.

[00:18:10] Sophie: security/compliance — do you have a SOC2 report we can share with procurement?
[00:18:15] Jordan: yes, we'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and our ISO attestation. also the market listing will include an explicit security questionnaire we can fill out with you.

[00:18:50] Omar: audit log format again — do you ship JSON lines? we need to ingest into our SIEM which expects structured events.
[00:18:56] Jordan: yes JSON lines with fields: timestamp, event_type, principal, resource, outcome. we'll send an example.

[00:19:30] Priya: back on runtime features — we have automatic prefix caching and token-level cost breakdowns in the console. For private installs the console can be on-prem or you can ship logs to your ELK.
[00:19:55] Aisha: mapping cost metrics to internal chargebacks is important — we'll want token breakdown by route/model.
[00:20:02] Jordan: we can export that as CSV or push to your metering endpoint.

[00:21:00] Liam: operational runbooks — we expect playbooks for upgrades and rollback. do you have a recommended canary cadence?
[00:21:06] Priya: we recommend small canary first (5%), monitor p95 and error rate for 24 hours, then 25% for another 24 hours, then full. for critical prod we also recommend a staged window outside business hours.

[00:21:45] Sophie: i'll add a note — product wants a demo of canary dashboard with our prompts during the lab.

[00:22:05] Priya: noted.

[00:22:30] Jordan: alright let's capture concrete next steps: 1) we'll share KMS integration doc, packaging checklist, and benchmark sheet; 2) priya will produce a helm values example; 3) orchardly to provision dev vpc and share CIDR + proxy/nat rules; 4) schedule 2-hour lab week of 6/15. Anything missing?
[00:22:55] Liam: please include the SBOM/image-signing requirements and marketplace submission timeline.
[00:23:00] Jordan: will do.

[00:23:30] Omar: one more Q — if we require HSM key attestations can redwood support a flow where we provide attestation only to runtime and the runtime rotates keys without central storage?
[00:23:41] Priya: yes that's the agent-driven flow — keys never leave your HSM, runtime requests short-lived wrapping keys via the agent. we'll detail the attestation flow in the runbook.

[00:24:10] Aisha: on image hardening, do you require specific CVE patch levels?
[00:24:16] Jordan: the marketplace security checklist lists minimum patch dates and SBOM scanning. We'll share the gating doc.

[00:25:00] Priya: technical note — for quantized kernels we often suggest enabling fused attention kernels and a specific CUDA version; we'll list those matrix entries. Sometimes inference perf is driven more by kernel selection than quant alone.

[00:26:10] Sophie: timeline recap: ship docs by 6/8, infra by 6/12, lab week of 6/15. Is that accurate?
[00:26:18] Jordan: yes that's what we discussed.

[00:27:00] Priya: ok any blockers from Orchardly side?
[00:27:05] Liam: main blocker is procurement sign-off on the pilot contract; sophie and omar are coordinating.
[00:27:12] Sophie: procurement has one question on data residency — want guarantee that logs stay in our VPC.
[00:27:18] Jordan: we can set retention to zero and push logs to your syslog collector — that should meet the requirement.

[00:28:10] Aisha: small ops question — how do upgrades handle schema changes in the local cache? we need migrations handled safely.
[00:28:18] Priya: we have migration hooks in our helm chart with preupgrade jobs, and we recommend running backups before upgrade. We'll include an upgrade playbook.

[00:29:05] Omar: do you have a support escalation path for 24/7?
[00:29:09] Jordan: for dedicated and private customers we offer premium support with 24/7 on-call and a named SE; pilot customers usually get business-hours support unless they opt in. That's something to agree in the pilot SOW.

[00:30:00] Priya: ok last technical deep dive point — observability agents: we emit spans compatible with opentelemetry and metrics to prometheus. For private installs we provide a prometheus scrape config and a grafana dashboard package.

[00:30:28] Aisha: perfect.

[00:31:00] Jordan: wrapping up — recap of action items (we'll email the list): send KMS runbook + helm chart, share benchmark sheet, orchardly to provision vpc, schedule lab. Anything else?
[00:31:18] Liam: include the CVE/SBOM gating.
[00:31:22] Jordan: got it.

[00:31:55] Sophie: thanks everyone — this was productive.
[00:31:58] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with links.

[00:32:10] (meeting ends, casual chatter and fade)

Post meeting notes: links to share: docs.redwood.ai/onprem-kms, github.com/redwood-inference/helm-examples/orchardly, drive:/orchardly/pilot-benchmarks (we'll email the actual links).

End transcript.
